SELECT
  'order cancellations' AS entity_type,
  COUNT(*) AS total_events,
  COUNT(*) FILTER (
    WHERE EXISTS (
      SELECT 1 FROM audit_log al
      WHERE al.entity_table = 'orders'
        AND al.entity_id = o.id
        AND al.tenant_id = o.tenant_id
    )
  ) AS events_with_match,
  ROUND(
    100.0 * COUNT(*) FILTER (
      WHERE EXISTS (
        SELECT 1 FROM audit_log al
        WHERE al.entity_table = 'orders'
          AND al.entity_id = o.id
          AND al.tenant_id = o.tenant_id
      )
    ) / NULLIF(COUNT(*), 0), 1
  ) AS coverage_rate_pct,
  COUNT(DISTINCT o.tenant_id) AS distinct_tenants
FROM orders o
WHERE o.status = 'cancelled'
  AND o.cancelled_at >= DATE '2023-01-01'
  AND o.cancelled_at < DATE '2026-01-01'

UNION ALL

SELECT
  'invoice voids' AS entity_type,
  COUNT(*) AS total_events,
  COUNT(*) FILTER (
    WHERE EXISTS (
      SELECT 1 FROM audit_log al
      WHERE al.entity_table = 'invoices'
        AND al.entity_id = i.id
        AND al.tenant_id = i.tenant_id
    )
  ) AS events_with_match,
  ROUND(
    100.0 * COUNT(*) FILTER (
      WHERE EXISTS (
        SELECT 1 FROM audit_log al
        WHERE al.entity_table = 'invoices'
          AND al.entity_id = i.id
          AND al.tenant_id = i.tenant_id
      )
    ) / NULLIF(COUNT(*), 0), 1
  ) AS coverage_rate_pct,
  COUNT(DISTINCT i.tenant_id) AS distinct_tenants
FROM invoices i
WHERE i.status = 'void'
  AND i.voided_at >= DATE '2023-01-01'
  AND i.voided_at < DATE '2026-01-01'

ORDER BY entity_type
note: Events are scoped to 2023-01-01..2025-12-31 using orders.cancelled_at / invoices.voided_at (the rows where that timestamp is null despite the terminal status are excluded from the count, since there's no other way to date them). Match test is an EXISTS on audit_log by (entity_table, entity_id, tenant_id) with any action — as requested, this only proves some audit trail exists for the row, not that the cancellation/void itself was the logged event; even 100% coverage would not confirm that.
